lessons.title: Technology
warmup: 💻 Gadgets
What technology do you use every day? / Har kuni nima ishlatasiz?
📱 How much time?
How much time do you spend on your phone? / Telefonda qancha vaqt?

x: My phone is my favourite device.
Don't look at the screen too long.
I searched for the answer online.
The phone connects to the internet.
The internet is a great invention.

grammar.rule: Present Perfect: **have/has + past participle** for experiences (ever/never)
ex: **Have you ever** searched for a recipe online?

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: I have ___ this video before. → a) seen b) see c) seeing

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: ever / you / a / drone / Have / used / ?

reading.title: My Phone and Me
reading.passage: My phone is my best friend — but sometimes it's a problem. I have used it for three years, and I have downloaded hundreds of apps. I have never lost it, thank goodness! I use it to search for information, chat with friends and take photos. But last week I looked at the screen for five hours! Now I have a new rule: no phone after nine o'clock. Technology is amazing, but I am the boss, not my phone.
qs: How long has the writer used his phone?
What does he use it for?
What new rule did he make?
What does 'I am the boss' mean?

listening.title: Two Friends on the Phone
qs: What has the girl downloaded?
What has the boy done this week?
What does the girl advise?
listening.script: Listen. Girl: 'I have downloaded a new language app. It's great!' Boy: 'Nice! I have watched five English videos this week.' Girl: 'Wow! I have never watched English videos.' Boy: 'You should try. Have you ever tried video calling?' Girl: 'Yes, I have. It's fun!'

writing.title: Technology in My Life
writing.task: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) using have/has: apps you have downloaded, things you have or haven't done.
writing.uz: Texnologiya haqida Present Perfect bilan yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What technology do you use daily?
My phone and my laptop.
What apps have you downloaded?
I have downloaded games and a dictionary.
Have you ever lost your phone?
Yes, but I found it!

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people: 'Have you ever used...?' Report. / 3 kishidan so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 technology words 3× · Grammar: 6 Present Perfect sentences · Reading: re-read 'My Phone and Me' · Speaking: discuss screen time with your family.
teacher: Introduce Present Perfect gently — B1 first taste.

lessons.title: Social Media
warmup: 📱 Apps
Which social media apps do you know? / Qaysi ilovalarni bilasiz?
👍 Your habits
How often do you check social media? / Qanchalik tez-tez?

x: Real life is more important than apps.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Online safety: → a) keep passwords secret b) share everything c) talk to strangers

reading.title: A Safe Account
reading.passage: Zarina loves social media. She posts photos of her paintings and reads the comments happily. But she is careful. Her account is private, so only her friends can see it. She never shares her password, not even with her best friend. She never posts her address or her school name. Last week, a stranger sent her a message. Zarina didn't reply — she blocked him and told her parents. 'Social media is fun,' she says, 'if you are smart.'
qs: What does Zarina post?
Why is her account private?
What did the stranger send?
What did Zarina do?

listening.title: Two Opinions
qs: What does the girl like about social media?
What does the boy think?
What rule do they agree on?
listening.script: Listen. Girl: 'I love social media! I see my friends' photos and learn new things.' Boy: 'Sometimes it's too much. People spend hours looking at screens.' Girl: 'That's true. But it's useful for school projects.' Boy: 'Let's agree: use it, but not too much.' Girl: 'Deal!'

writing.title: Social Media Rules
writing.task: Write a set of 5 safety rules for using social media, using should/shouldn't.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: How much time do you spend online?
About two hours a day.
What do you like about social media?
I see my friends' news.
What are the dangers?
Strangers and too much time.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Check your account privacy settings with your parents. / Profil sozlamalarini tekshiring.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 social media words 3× · Grammar: 5 safety rules · Reading: re-read 'A Safe Account' · Speaking: discuss online safety with your family.
teacher: Real and relevant topic — students engage deeply.

lessons.title: Giving Opinions
goals: 💭 Give your opinion: 'I think... / In my opinion...'
🤔 Ask for opinions: 'What do you think?'
warmup: 💭 Opinions
Do you think English is important? Why? / Ingliz tili muhimmi?
🤔 Debate warm-up
Phone or computer — which is better? / Telefon yoki kompyuter?

x: I think it's a good idea.
In my opinion, books are better than films.
I think so because it's cheaper.

grammar.rule: Opinions: **I think / In my opinion / I agree / I disagree** + reason with because
ex: **I think** English is important **because** it helps you travel.
Ingliz tili muhim, chunki sayohatda yordam beradi.
**I agree with** you. / **I disagree —** I think it's expensive.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: You agree: → a) I agree with you b) I disagree c) I think not

reading.title: Books or Films?
reading.passage: Yesterday my class discussed a question: books or films? 'I think books are better,' said Gulnora. 'When you read, you imagine everything yourself. Films show you one person's picture.' 'In my opinion, films win,' said Jasur. 'They are quicker — two hours, and the story is over. Also, the music makes it exciting.' 'That's a good point,' said Gulnora, 'but a book stays with you for weeks.' The teacher smiled: 'The best opinion is to enjoy both.'
qs: Why does Gulnora prefer books?
Why does Jasur prefer films?
What did Gulnora say about books staying?
What did the teacher say?

listening.title: Opinions About City Life
qs: What does the first speaker think about city life?
What does the second speaker disagree with?
What do they agree on?
listening.script: Listen. Speaker 1: 'In my opinion, city life is the best. There are cinemas, shops and many jobs.' Speaker 2: 'I disagree. Cities are too crowded and noisy. The village is calmer.' Speaker 1: 'But you must travel far for work.' Speaker 2: 'That's true. Both places have good points.'

writing.title: My Opinion
writing.task: Write your opinion (5-7 sentences) about a topic: 'Books or films?' or 'City or village?' Use opinion phrases.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What do you think about homework?
I think it's useful, but not too much.
In your opinion, what's the best sport?
Football, because it's exciting.
Do you agree with me?
Yes, I do. / Sorry, I disagree.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask your family's opinion on a topic tonight. Report 2 opinions. / Oilangizdan fikr so'rang.

lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 opinion words 3× · Grammar: 6 opinion sentences with reasons · Reading: re-read 'Books or Films?' · Speaking: share opinions with your family.
teacher: Opinions are the core of B1 speaking.

lessons.title: Agreeing and Disagreeing
warmup: 🤝 Agree or disagree?
'Pizza is the best food.' Do you agree? / Rozimisiz?
👎 Polite words
How do you disagree without fighting? / Qanday xushmuomala bo'lasiz?

x: That's true. However, I have a question.

grammar.rule: Agree: **I agree / Exactly / That's true** · Disagree: **I'm afraid I disagree / I see your point, but...**
ex: **I'm afraid I disagree** — prices are going up.
**I see your point, but** I think it's too expensive.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: That's true. ___ , I have a question. (However/In fact)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: Polite disagreement: → a) I'm afraid I disagree b) You're wrong c) No!

reading.title: A School Discussion
reading.passage: Our class discussed school uniforms. 'I completely agree with uniforms,' said Madina. 'They make everyone equal.' 'That's true,' said Timur. 'However, I think students should choose their own style.' 'In fact, many countries don't have uniforms,' added Kamola. 'Perhaps we should try a year without them.' The teacher nodded. 'You all have good points. A respectful discussion is the best way to learn.' Everyone left with something to think about.
qs: Why does Madina like uniforms?
What does Timur say however?
What does Kamola say about other countries?
What did the teacher say about the discussion?

listening.title: The Debate
qs: What does the first speaker agree with?
What does the second speaker disagree with?
How do they end the discussion?
listening.script: Listen. Speaker 1: 'In my opinion, animals should not live in zoos.' Speaker 2: 'I see your point, but zoos protect animals from danger.' Speaker 1: 'Perhaps, but cages are too small.' Speaker 2: 'That's true. However, many zoos are improving.' Speaker 1: 'Let's agree to respect both views.' Speaker 2: 'Agreed!'

writing.title: Agree and Disagree
writing.task: Write 4 sentences: 2 agreements and 2 polite disagreements about a topic you choose.
writing.uz: Rozi bo'lish va rozi bo'lmaslik gaplari yozing.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What do you think about homework?
I agree — it helps us practice.
Is it good to have a pet?
I'm afraid I disagree — they need time.
Do you like online school?
I see your point, but I prefer class.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Have a discussion with your family and use 3 polite phrases. / Oilangiz bilan muhokama qiling.

quiz: What is a polite way to disagree?
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 discussion words 3× · Grammar: 4 agree/disagree sentences · Reading: re-read 'A School Discussion' · Speaking: discuss with your family politely.
teacher: Teach the polite chunks — crucial for B1.

lessons.title: Environment
warmup: 🌍 Our planet
Why should we protect nature? / Tabiatni nima uchun asrash kerak?
♻️ Problems
What environmental problems do you know? / Qanday muammolar bor?

x: Air pollution is a big problem.
Please put the rubbish in the bin.

grammar.rule: Suggestions: **should + verb** · **We must + verb** for strong obligation · problem → solution
ex: People **must stop** throwing rubbish in the river.
Odamlar daryoga axlat tashlashni to'xtatishi kerak.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: You ___ throw rubbish in the river. (mustn't/must)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: To help the planet: → a) recycle plastic b) throw plastic in the river c) waste water

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: in / don't / river / the / throw / rubbish / .

reading.title: The River That Was Clean
reading.passage: Twenty years ago, the river near our town was clean. People swam in it and caught fish. Then factories came. They threw waste into the water, and pollution grew. The fish disappeared. Our class decided to help. We organized a cleaning day — students, teachers and parents collected rubbish from the banks. We also talked to the factory. Now it cleans its water. 'Small actions change big problems,' our teacher said. The river is slowly coming back.
qs: What was the river like twenty years ago?
What happened when factories came?
What did the class organize?
What did they do about the factory?

listening.title: Eco Tips
qs: What should the family do with plastic bottles?
How should they save energy?
What advice about shopping?
listening.script: Listen. Today's eco tips. First, you should recycle plastic bottles — don't throw them in the bin. Second, turn off the lights when you leave a room; it saves energy. Third, take a cloth bag to the market instead of plastic bags. And remember: don't waste water while brushing your teeth. Small steps, big change!

writing.title: My Eco Plan
writing.task: Write 5 things you can do to help the environment, using should/must.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What's the biggest problem in your area?
Air pollution from cars.
What should we do about it?
Use buses and bikes more.
Do you recycle at home?
Not yet, but we should start.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Do one eco action this week: recycle, save water or energy. Report. / Bitta ekologik ish qiling.

quiz: Name 3 ways to help the environment.
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 environment words 3× · Grammar: 5 eco suggestions · Reading: re-read 'The River That Was Clean' · Speaking: discuss ecology with your family.
teacher: This feeds L86 (first conditional) and L87 (debate).

lessons.title: First Conditional
goals: 🔀 Form the first conditional (If + present, will)
🌧️ Make predictions: 'If it rains, I'll stay home'
warmup: 🔀 If... then...
'If I study, I will pass.' What about you? / Agar... bo'lsa...?
🌦️ Weather plans
What will you do if it rains today? / Yomg'ir yog'sa nima qilasiz?

x: If I study, I will pass.
Stay home instead of going out.
If it's sunny tomorrow, we'll go.
If I pass, I'll be happy.
If I fail, I'll try again.
If I wake up late, I'll run to school.

grammar.rule: First conditional: **If + present, will + verb** (real future possibility)
ex: **If you study**, you **will pass** the test.
**If we hurry**, we **will catch** the bus.
mistake: Wrong: *If it will rain, I stay.*
Right: *If it rains, I will stay.*

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: If we hurry, we ___ catch the bus. (will/are)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: If I feel tired, ___ → a) I will sleep b) I sleep c) I slept

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: if / stay / I'll / rains / home / it / .
you / will / study / if / pass / you / .

reading.title: The Weather Test
reading.passage: The school trip to the mountains was on Saturday. But the weather was uncertain. 'If it rains, we will cancel the trip,' said the teacher. 'If it is cloudy, we will still go, but we'll take umbrellas. If it is sunny, we'll have a picnic!' The students waited nervously. On Friday night, the forecast said: sunny! 'If we go, I'll take my camera,' said Anvar. 'If my camera works, I'll take a photo of everyone!' Everyone laughed. The trip was on.
qs: What will happen if it rains?
What will they do if it is cloudy?
What will Anvar do if they go?
What did the forecast say?

listening.title: If I Have Time
qs: What will the girl do if she has time?
What will she do if her friend comes?
What will happen if the shop is closed?
listening.script: Listen. Girl: 'If I have time after school, I'll go to the bookshop.' Friend: 'If I come with you, will you help me choose a book?' Girl: 'Of course! If the bookshop is closed, we'll go to the library instead.' Friend: 'Great. If we meet at 4, we'll have plenty of time.'

writing.title: My Plans with If
writing.task: Write 5 first conditional sentences about your plans this week.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What will you do if it rains?
I'll read a book.
What will you do if you get home early?
I'll help my mother.
What happens if you wake up late?
I'll run to school!

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Make 2 'if' predictions for tomorrow and check them. / Ertaga uchun 2 bashorat qiling.

quiz: Correct: 'If it will rain, I stay.'
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 conditional words 3× · Grammar: 6 first conditional sentences · Reading: re-read 'The Weather Test' · Speaking: make if-plans with your family.
teacher: Teach the pattern as a formula: If+present, will+verb.
This is a key B1 grammar — used in L97 too.

lessons.title: Debate Workshop
goals: 🎤 Debate a topic in a team
Hurmat bilan tinglash va javob berish
warmup: 🎤 Debate topics
Name 2 topics people argue about. / Nima haqida bahslashiladi?
🤔 One opinion
Say one strong opinion you have. / Bitta qat'iy fikr ayting.

practice.title: The Debate Plan
items: Choose a topic: 'Social media is good for students' or 'Homework should be smaller'. / Mavzu tanlang.
Split into two teams: For and Against. / Ikkiga bo'ling.
Each team writes 3 reasons with examples. / 3 ta dalil yozing.
Team 1 speaks (1 minute), Team 2 listens. / Jamoa 1 gapiradi.
Team 2 responds politely. Then Team 1 responds. / Javob bering.
Judges decide the winner. / Hakamlar hal qiladi.

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: You disagree with a speaker: → a) I see your point, but... b) You're wrong! c) Silence

speaking.title: Your Argument
speaking.body: Present your argument: opinion + 2 reasons + 1 conditional sentence. / Fikringizni asoslang.

speaking.title: The Cross-Examination
speaking.body: Ask your opponent one question. Answer theirs politely. / Raqibingizga savol bering.

speaking.title: The Vote
speaking.body: Judges give feedback and the class votes. / Hakamlar fikr beradi.

quiz: What is a good way to disagree?
lessons.homework: Write your final argument (6-8 sentences) for your side of the debate. / Yakuniy dalilingizni yozing.
teacher: Workshop: debates are excellent B1 practice.
Use 'I see your point, but' structures.

lessons.title: Speaking Circle: Opinions
warmup: 💬 Opinion quick round
Finish: 'In my opinion, English is...' / Gapni tugating.
🤝 Agree/Disagree
Say a sentence; your partner agrees or disagrees. / Bir gap ayting.

practice.title: Opinion Cards
items: Should students have phones at school? / Maktabda telefon bo'lishi kerakmi?
Is city life better than village life? / Shahar hayoti yaxshimi?
Should homework exist? / Uy vazifasi kerakmi?
Are pets good for children? / Uy hayvonlari foydalimi?
Is social media more good than bad? / Ijtimoiy tarmoq foydalimi?

speaking.title: My Strong Opinion
speaking.body: Speak for 2 minutes on one topic: opinion, 2 reasons, 1 example. / Kuchli fikringiz haqida gapiring.

speaking.title: The Panel
speaking.body: Form a panel of 3. Present opinions, ask questions, vote on the best view. / Uch kishilik panel tuzing.

speaking.title: Active Listening
speaking.body: Summarize one opinion you heard in 2 sentences. / Bitta fikrni xulosalang.

quiz: Give one reason for your opinion.
lessons.homework: Write your opinion on one topic (8-10 sentences) with reasons. Practice speaking it. / Fikringizni yozing.
teacher: Builds confidence for B1 speaking exams.

lessons.title: City vs Countryside
warmup: 🌆 City life
What do you love about the city? / Shaharda nimani sevasiz?
🌾 Countryside life
What do you love about the countryside? / Qishloqda?

x: More job opportunities in the city.
An advantage of the city is transport.

grammar.rule: Discuss pros and cons: **advantage/disadvantage + is** · **on the one hand / on the other hand**
grammar.uz: Afzallik/kamchilik: 'on the one hand... on the other hand'
ex: **On the one hand**, cities have more jobs.
Bir tomondan, shaharda ko'proq ish bor.
**On the other hand**, the countryside is peaceful.
**An advantage of** the village is fresh air.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: An ___ of the city is transport. (advantage/disadvantage)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: A disadvantage of the village: → a) far from shops b) clean air c) quiet

reading.title: Where Is Home?
reading.passage: My grandmother lives in a village, and I visit her every summer. On the one hand, the city has more facilities: big hospitals, modern schools and cinemas. On the other hand, the village gives me something the city cannot: fresh air, quiet nights and the smell of fresh bread. The city is convenient, but the countryside is peaceful. When I grow up, I want to work in the city but have a small house in the village. That would be perfect!
qs: What facilities does the city have?
What does the village give the writer?
What does the writer want when he grows up?
What does 'perfect' mean to the writer?

listening.title: The Decision
qs: Where does the woman want to live?
What does the man prefer?
What do they agree about?
listening.script: Listen. Woman: 'I want to move to the village. Life is calmer there.' Man: 'But we need the city for work and school.' Woman: 'That's true. However, we could live on the edge of the city.' Man: 'Good point — we get nature and facilities!' Woman: 'Exactly! The best of both worlds.'

writing.title: City or Countryside?
writing.task: Write a paragraph (6-8 sentences) comparing city and countryside: advantages and disadvantages, and your choice.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: Where do you prefer to live?
I prefer the city.
What's the best thing about your home area?
The people and the food.
What's a disadvantage?
The traffic in the mornings.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Ask 3 people if they prefer city or village. Report their reasons. / 3 kishidan so'rang.

quiz: Fill: 'An ___ of the village is fresh air.' (advantage/disadvantage)
Fill: '___ the other hand, it's quiet.' (On/In)
Name one advantage and one disadvantage of the city.
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 city/countryside words 3× · Grammar: 6 pros/cons sentences · Reading: re-read 'Where Is Home?' · Speaking: discuss with your family.
teacher: Teach 'on the one hand / on the other hand' chunks.
This is classic B1 exam material.

lessons.title: Global Cultures
warmup: 🌏 World quiz
Name a country and one thing it is famous for. / Mamlakat va uning mashhur tomoni.
🎎 Your culture
What is Uzbekistan famous for? / O'zbekiston nima bilan mashhur?

x: Salomlashish odatlari har joyda har xil.
There is a flower festival in spring.
We exchange gifts on this day.
Our world is diverse and beautiful.
We live in a global world.

grammar.rule: Describe customs: **In + country, people + verb** · **It is a tradition to + verb**
ex: **In Japan, people bow** when they meet.
**In Italy, people celebrate** with big family dinners.
Italiyada katta oilaviy kechki ovqatlar bilan nishonlanadi.
**It is a tradition to** drink tea in Uzbekistan.

practice.title: Fill in the Gaps
items: It is a ___ to drink tea. (tradition/traditional)

practice.title: Circle the Answer
items: In Japan, people ___ when they meet. → a) bow b) shake c) kiss

practice.title: Build the Sentence
items: tradition / tea / is / to / drink / it / a / .

reading.title: A Festival in My School
reading.passage: Our school held an international festival. Each class chose a country. My class chose Japan. We learned that in Japan, people bow when they greet, and they take off their shoes at home. We decorated our corner with paper flowers and taught everyone to write 'hello' in Japanese. The Korean class showed a traditional dance. The Turkish class served tea in small glasses. At the end, our teacher said: 'Look at us — different clothes, different food, but one happy school. That is what a global world should be.'
qs: What did the writer's class choose?
What did they learn about Japan?
What did the Korean class show?
What did the teacher say at the end?

listening.title: Customs Around the World
qs: What do people do in Thailand?
What do people in Brazil love?
What did the speaker learn?
listening.script: Listen. Today I learned about customs. In Thailand, people press their hands together to say hello. In Brazil, people love festivals and dancing — especially in February. In some places, it is rude to refuse food. Every custom is different, but all of them show respect. Learning about them makes the world friendlier.

writing.title: A Custom in My Country
writing.task: Write a paragraph (5-7 sentences) about a custom in Uzbekistan, using 'In our country, people...'.

speaking.title: Talk with a Partner
table: What is your country famous for?
Our food and hospitality.
What is a custom you love?
Greeting elders first.
What customs surprised you?
In Japan, people take off their shoes.

speaking.title: Real-life Mission
speaking.body: Tell your family one custom of another country. / Oilangizga boshqa xalq odatini ayting.

quiz: Fill: 'It is a ___ to drink tea.' (tradition/traditional)
Name one custom of another country.
lessons.homework: Vocabulary: 10 culture words 3× · Grammar: 6 sentences about customs · Reading: re-read 'A Festival in My School' · Speaking: share a custom with your family.
teacher: Celebrate the diversity of the class.
Watch for present continuous for habits.
This leads to L91 (famous people) and L93 (documentary).
